transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I'm here mainly because... for a long time now, my sleep has just been really broken. I fall into bed completely exhausted, but then I wake up to every little sound in the house. And then I'm always awake before my alarm even goes off, just feeling like I never really rested at all.
Has anyone who sleeps near you ever told you that you snore loudly, gasp, or seem to stop breathing for a moment during sleep?
No, no one's ever mentioned anything like that to me. I don't think I snore, or at least, I haven't been told that I do.
Over the past few weeks, have you noticed feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yes, I have. It's... well, most days I just feel like the color has gone out of things. Even when I'm sitting at Sunday dinner with my family, or looking at art I used to enjoy, it's just flat. And I find myself having to work really hard not to tear up, and there's no clear reason for it. I just feel sad.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, or has it been going on for two years or more?
It's been... well, definitely longer than a few weeks. This has been going on since my mother-in-law moved in with us, so that's been a little over two years ago now.
Over these past two years, has there ever been a stretch of two months or longer when you felt essentially back to your normal self, without the sadness or flatness?
No, I haven't. I don't think there's been a time... definitely not for two whole months, anyway. It's just been pretty constant this whole time. I haven't really felt back to normal at all.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight—either a marked increase or decrease—during this time?

Yeah, I really don't have much of an appetite anymore. I mostly just end up picking at whatever I make for everyone else, or... well, I might just grab a piece of toast after my shift and leave it at that. Because of that, my clothes have been hanging a lot looser on me lately, even though I'm not actually trying to lose weight.
During this time, have you been having thoughts that you're worthless, or feeling excessively guilty about things, even minor ones?

No, not really. I don't feel worthless... and I don't think I feel excessively guilty about things, either. I mean, I know I'm doing the best I can with my patients at work and taking care of things at home. It's just... I just feel down all the time. But no, I wouldn't say I have thoughts like that.
During this same two-year period, have you noticed trouble concentrating or making decisions, like at work with your patients or at home?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with that. I mean, my job takes a lot of focus, making sure my patients get their meds and all, and I haven't messed any of that up. And at home, things just run like they always do. I can still make decisions fine, it's just... I just don't have much energy for it all. But my concentration is okay.

Within these past two years, has there been any stretch of at least two weeks where your mood and other symptoms became noticeably worse than your usual baseline, almost like a more intense low point?

No, I don't think so. It hasn't really... spiked or gotten intensely worse like that at any point. It's honestly just been this same, steady low the whole time. Every day just kind of feels like the last one, so... no, I wouldn't say there was a specific stretch where it suddenly dipped lower than my usual. It's just always there.
During this time, have you had any thoughts about death, or thoughts of hurting yourself or that you'd be better off not being alive?

No, nothing like that. I don't... I've never had any thoughts about hurting myself or anything. Even with feeling down all the time, I definitely don't want to die or feel like I shouldn't be here. So, no, I haven't had any of those kinds of thoughts.
